vectors.title: Keys with special characters list correctly, read back their bodies and accept ACLs
Keys containing URL-encoding-like characters round-trip literally
vectors.description: Keys that look percent-encoded or contain '+', '?' and '#' must be stored and retrieved literally, not decoded.

vectors.title: Path-traversal-like keys and Windows reserved names round-trip
vectors.description: Keys containing ../ or ..\ sequences must be stored literally (no path normalization); Windows reserved device names are ordinary keys.

vectors.title: Keys containing CR/LF and escape control characters round-trip
vectors.description: The original also tried a key containing a NUL (0x00) byte, accepting either success or InvalidArgument rejection; that case is omitted because the accept-or-reject disjunction is not expressible.

vectors.title: Slash-only keys and a 1024-byte maximum-length key round-trip
Key longer than 1024 bytes is rejected
vectors.description: The original accepted KeyTooLong* or InvalidRequest; AWS returns KeyTooLongError.

vectors.title: Unicode object key round-trip
Object key containing '+' is listable by literal '+' prefix and HEADable
vectors.description: The source test branches on an SDK capability flag for legacy '+'-as-space URL encoding; the correct S3 behavior (default branch) is that '+' in a key is a literal plus sign.

vectors.title: Real-world object keys mixing paths, dates, '@', parentheses, colons, '#' and brackets round-trip
vectors.description: Listing order assertion relies on S3's guaranteed ascending UTF-8 binary key order.

vectors.title: Path-like object keys (nested, leading/trailing/double slashes, directory markers) list correctly
vectors.description: Listing order assertion relies on S3's guaranteed ascending UTF-8 binary key order.

vectors.title: Object keys with 24 common special characters can be created, listed and read back
vectors.description: Listing order assertion relies on S3's guaranteed ascending UTF-8 binary key order.

vectors.title: Object keys with non-ASCII Unicode characters (CJK, accents, Cyrillic, emoji) list correctly
vectors.description: Listing order assertion relies on S3's guaranteed ascending UTF-8 binary key order.

vectors.title: Object keys requiring URL encoding round-trip through put, get and list
Keys with URL-special ASCII characters round-trip through PutObject/GetObject
vectors.description: Space, plus, percent, question mark, hash, ampersand, equals and at-sign in object keys. The original accepted InvalidArgument rejection as an alternative outcome for lenient vendors; AWS S3 accepts all of these keys, so the vector asserts the round-trip.

vectors.title: Path-separator variations in keys are stored as-is and listable by prefix
vectors.description: Double/triple slashes, leading slash, dot and dot-dot segments must not be normalized: each key appears verbatim in a prefix listing (prefixes are the first five characters of the key, as in the original test).

vectors.title: A raw space and a percent-encoded space are distinct object keys
vectors.description: 'test space.txt' and 'test%20space.txt' are two different objects. The original also tolerated normalization to a single form; AWS S3 stores both distinctly, so the listing asserts exactly the two keys.

vectors.title: UTF-8 international keys round-trip through PutObject/GetObject
vectors.description: Accented Latin, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese and Korean keys. The original accepted InvalidArgument rejection as an alternative outcome; AWS S3 accepts any UTF-8 key, so the vector asserts the round-trip.

vectors.title: Spaces and percent sequences in directory and file parts are accepted
vectors.description: PutObject with reserved characters at different path positions, then ListObjectsV2 with the directory part as Prefix and '/' Delimiter. The original recorded the listing outcome without failing on absence, so the converted steps assert only that both operations succeed.

vectors.title: Query-string-like characters in keys are accepted and retrievable
vectors.description: Keys containing '?', '&', '=' and '#' sequences that resemble query strings or fragments must not be interpreted as such. The original accepted InvalidArgument rejection as an alternative outcome; AWS S3 accepts these keys.

vectors.title: Object keys are case-sensitive
vectors.description: GetObject with the case-swapped form of each stored key must fail. The original accepted any error; AWS S3 returns 404 NoSuchKey since the case-swapped key does not exist.

vectors.title: An 819-character key round-trips
vectors.description: A long key approaching URL length limits (within the 1024-byte S3 key limit). The original accepted KeyTooLong/RequestURITooLong as an alternative outcome; AWS S3 accepts keys up to 1024 bytes, so the vector asserts the round-trip.

vectors.title: CreateMultipartUpload preserves keys with non-ASCII (Greek, Chinese) characters
